title: Prevalence, Severity, and Distribution of Permanent Tooth Agenesis among Children Attending a University Pediatric Dental Clinic in Turkey: A Retrospective Radiographic Study
content: Background/Objectives: To determine the prevalence, severity, and tooth-type distribution of nonsyndromic permanent tooth agenesis among children attending a university pediatric dental clinic in Turkey. Methods: Records and diagnostic radiographs of 7,109 children aged 6-15 years who attended Karadeniz Technical University between January 2019 and January 2021 were evaluated retrospectively. Children with syndromic or generalized developmental conditions and radiographs of insufficient quality were excluded. Agenesis was diagnosed when a permanent tooth germ was absent radiographically and extraction or acquired loss was not indicated; third molars were excluded. Prevalence, severity, and tooth-type distribution were summarized descriptively with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Permanent tooth agenesis was identified in 546 children (7.68%; 95% CI: 7.08-8.32), including 288 girls and 258 boys. Overall, 1,150 permanent teeth were absent. One or two teeth were missing in 439 children (80.4%), three to five in 78 (14.3%), and six or more in 29 (5.3%). Mandibular second premolars were most frequently absent (32.7%), followed by maxillary lateral incisors (26.1%) and maxillary second premolars (17.9%). Conclusions: Permanent tooth agenesis affected approximately one in thirteen children in this clinic-based sample. Most affected children had one or two missing teeth, with agenesis concentrated in second premolars and maxillary lateral incisors.
